architecture_decisions.recommendation: Downgraded OpenTelemetry SDK from v1.40.0 to v1.37.0 (contrib/datadog) and v1.27.0 (contrib/opentelemetry/test) to address CI flakiness issues
architecture_decisions.rationale: The OpenTelemetry v1.40.0 upgrade introduced instability in the CI pipeline, causing test failures that blocked the v1.41.0 release. Reverting to previously stable versions ensures reliable test execution while maintaining observability functionality.
alternatives_considered: Fix tests to work with v1.40.0
Upgrade to a newer patch version

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Reverted Go version from 1.24.0 to 1.23.0 and added explicit toolchain specification (go1.23.6) in contrib/opentelemetry and test modules
architecture_decisions.rationale: The OpenTelemetry v1.40.0 upgrade required Go 1.24.0. Reverting dependencies necessitated reverting the Go version as well to maintain compatibility. Explicit toolchain specification ensures consistent builds across environments.
alternatives_considered: Update all modules to a consistent Go version

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed conditional nil-checking assertions in integration tests and simplified retry logic in worker deployment tests that were added during the v1.40.0 upgrade
architecture_decisions.rationale: The test modifications introduced with v1.40.0 were either unnecessary or contributed to flakiness. Removing conditional assertions (assert.NotNil checks) and complex retry logic reduces test complexity and potential failure points.
alternatives_considered: Keep test modifications but fix underlying issues

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Downgraded related dependencies including go.opentelemetry.io/auto/sdk, golang.org/x/sys, and test dependencies (stretchr/testify, google/go-cmp, uber/goleak) to versions compatible with OpenTelemetry v1.27.0-1.37.0
architecture_decisions.rationale: OpenTelemetry SDK upgrades often require coordinated updates of transitive dependencies. Reverting these ensures a consistent, tested dependency graph that worked reliably before the upgrade.
alternatives_considered: Keep newer versions of transitive dependencies

implementation_summary:
The implementation focused on stabilizing the CI pipeline by systematically reverting the OpenTelemetry SDK upgrade from v1.40.0 to previously stable versions. This involved coordinated changes across multiple modules: contrib/datadog was downgraded to v1.37.0, while contrib/opentelemetry and test modules were reverted to v1.27.0-1.28.0. The downgrade required reverting Go versions from 1.24.0 to 1.23.0 with explicit toolchain specifications to maintain compatibility.

Key patterns include maintaining dependency consistency across the monorepo - when OpenTelemetry was downgraded, related dependencies like go.opentelemetry.io/auto/sdk, golang.org/x/sys, and test utilities (stretchr/testify, google/go-cmp) were also reverted to versions known to work together. This holistic approach prevents version mismatches that could cause runtime issues.

The changes integrate with the existing codebase by targeting the specific areas affected by the original upgrade: dependency files (go.mod/go.sum) and test files that were modified during the upgrade. The test modifications removed were identified as potential sources of flakiness - specifically, unnecessary conditional nil checks in integration tests and overly complex retry logic in worker deployment tests. By reverting these, test reliability is improved without sacrificing coverage.

This rollback strategy prioritizes stability for the upcoming v1.41.0 release while leaving the door open for a more carefully managed OpenTelemetry upgrade in the future. The approach demonstrates pragmatic dependency management where stability trumps being on the latest versions when release timelines are at stake.
